record.original_question: If K(n, R) denotes the smallest size of a covering code of length n and covering radius R, is it always true for R ≠ n that K(n + 2, R + 1) ≤ K(n, R)?

evidence.quote: The smallest size of a covering code of length n and covering radius R is denoted by K(n, R).
Open Question 12.3. Is K(n + 2, R + 1) ≤ K(n, R) for all R ≠ n?[18].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers n ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ R ≤ n, a binary covering code of length n and covering radius R is a subset C ⊆ {0,1}^n such that every vector x ∈ {0,1}^n lies within Hamming distance R of some codeword c ∈ C. Let K(n, R) denote the smallest possible cardinality of such a code. 

Determine whether, for every pair of integers (n, R) with 0 ≤ R < n, the inequality
   K(n + 2, R + 1) ≤ K(n, R)
holds.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that the inequality K(n+2, R+1) ≤ K(n, R) is known to hold for sufficiently large n (via density/covering radius results in the covering-code literature), but a proof valid for all (n, R) with R ≠ n does not appear to be established, so the full conjecture appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Covering Radius — Survey and Recent Results
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of bounds and inequalities for K(n,R), including monotonicity-type relations.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys list inequalities relating K(n,R) at different parameters but the precise relation K(n+2,R+1) ≤ K(n,R) is discussed as a conjectural monotonicity property.

status_evidence.title: Inequalities for covering codes
status_evidence.snippet: Paper on inequalities among K(n,R) values.
status_evidence.claim: Known inequalities provide partial results toward the K(n+2,R+1) ≤ K(n,R) conjecture, established for large n.
